newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - FTSE active as UK stocks duck and dive.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - FTSE active as UK stocks duck and dive.

text.p: In a roller coaster day in the UK stock market, the bigger deals on Friday were in the FTSE 100 index options, dealers said.
Volatility trades as well as a mix of long and short positions were the main deals following this morning's expiry of the July index contracts.
One trader expecting the market to rise over the summer months hedged a long futures position by buying out-of-the-money puts and selling out-of-the-money calls in a long cylinder strategy.
The deal was to buy September FTSE futures at 4960 as well as 4,000 September 4825 puts at around 83p and to sell 4,000 September 5025 calls at prices near 63p.
It enables the trader to make a profit -- less 20p for the net cost of the options -- if FTSE futures rally up to 5025 when the short calls will be assigned.
And if futures prices fall below 4825, the losses from the long futures position can be cut by exercising the put options.
One large volatility trade in FTSE involved selling a call spread against futures. The spread concerned selling December 5125 calls at 150p and buying 1,000 December 5525 calls at 36p.
This spread was hedged by buying September futures at 4920 and the overall deal will make a profit if market volatility reduces.
As the market fell back, one large straight options deal was struck by selling 1,000 August 5100 calls at 46p. A more bearish deal was executed when one dealer bought 500 August 4000 puts at 2p.
By 1355 GMT, cash FTSE had slithered down 35.4 to 4913.6 while September FTSE futures had slumped 63 points to 4917.
